subject.title: iPhone Continuity Camera `--facing front` always uses rear camera

question: Should macOS camera capture keep `deviceId` as an exact selector when `facing` is also provided for an iPhone Continuity Camera device that reports `position: unspecified`?
rationale: The current implementation treats `deviceId` as exact, while the issue expects `facing` to choose a lens behind that device; automation cannot choose that compatibility contract without maintainer intent and live AVFoundation proof.

options.title: Keep device id exact
options.body: Preserve exact `deviceId` targeting and add a diagnostic or docs limitation if live proof shows Continuity Camera exposes only one selectable camera.

options.title: Add supported lens selection
options.body: If live AVFoundation proof shows a supported front/back selector for the same iPhone device, implement that narrow macOS path with tests and docs.

options.title: Let facing override device id
options.body: Change selector precedence so `facing` can replace an explicit device id, accepting compatibility risk for existing multi-camera users.

recommendation.title: Keep device id exact
recommendation.body: Preserve exact `deviceId` targeting and add a diagnostic or docs limitation if live proof shows Continuity Camera exposes only one selectable camera.

likelyOwner.reason: The camera device-selection feature and adjacent macOS camera refactors most strongly trace to this history.
